content.overview: Section 242 empowers the Tribunal, if it is satisfied that the company's affairs are oppressive or prejudicial, to make any order it thinks fit to bring an end to the matters complained of.
content.glance: Section 242 empowers the Tribunal, if it is satisfied that the company's affairs are oppressive or prejudicial, to make any order it thinks fit to bring an end to the matters complained of.
content.study: If the Tribunal finds that the company's affairs have been or are being conducted in a manner prejudicial or oppressive, and that winding up would unfairly prejudice members but is otherwise justified, it may pass any order to end the matters complained of. Orders can regulate future conduct, set aside or modify transactions and agreements, remove or appoint directors, and provide for purchase of shares. The order is the remedial counterpart of a section 241 application.

sections.heading: Jurisdiction to order
sections.body: The Tribunal must be satisfied of prejudicial or oppressive conduct and that winding up would unfairly prejudice members.

sections.heading: Range of orders
sections.body: Regulation of conduct, setting aside transactions, termination or modification of agreements, removal of directors, and purchase of shares.
